body.heading: Stand them up
paragraphs: Stand each domino on its end, close to the next one — about half a domino's length apart. Too far apart and the fall cannot jump the gap.
A curving trail is harder than a straight one. Each domino must aim at the middle of the next, like tiny falling soldiers in a parade.

body.heading: The one-push rule
paragraphs: When the whole trail is standing, push only the first domino. If your spacing is right, the fall travels all the way to the end, clickety-clickety-click.
If the trail stops, you have found a gap or a crooked domino. Fix it and try again. Engineers call this testing.

body.heading: Why it works
paragraphs: Each standing domino holds a little bit of falling energy. When it falls, it gives that energy to the next one, like passing a message down a line.
A tiny push at the start can topple a hundred dominoes — one small cause can make a very big effect.

takeaway: A domino trail passes falling energy from piece to piece, so one small push can topple the whole line.
materials: Dominoes, wooden blocks, or paperback books
safetyNotes: Use light dominoes or blocks that cannot hurt toes. Keep the trail away from breakable things.
screenFreeExtension: Build a trail that splits in two and topples both ways from one push.
